findings.title: Known diagnostics and protocol evidence are excluded from the no-replay proof
findings.observation: The proof collector reads result metadata, observation, observation metadata, and one accessibilityAction nesting. It does not add diagnostics, diagnostics.transport, ToolObservation.evidence, or ToolError.evidence to attempted/effect/action/code consistency checks; diagnostics transport is consulted only for requestDispatched.
findings.trigger: A backend reports a valid-looking accessibility_action_unsupported proof in direct payloads while a known diagnostics or protocol evidence container says actionAttempted=false, reports a conflicting field, or is malformed.
findings.impact: A shared caller can execute accessibility_action and then click, Return, focus, or another strategy even though the first outcome is contradictory, violating the no-replay boundary.

evidence.description: The real _AccessibilityWorker -> ComputerUseClient -> WeChat click phase returned success with operations ['accessibility_action', 'click'] while raw diagnostics reported actionAttempted=false and requestDispatched=true.
The collector stops after one nested action mapping, whereas request-dispatch extraction separately recognizes diagnostics.transport as a known evidence container.
The feature contract requires camel/snake aliases in observation, metadata, nested action payloads, diagnostics, and transport records to be presence-sensitive and fail closed.

findings.remediation: Define and implement one presence-sensitive traversal of every supported public, metadata, nested action, diagnostics, transport, ToolObservation.evidence, and ToolError.evidence container. Reject malformed containers and any conflicting attempted/dispatch copy before every shared fallback.
findings.verification: Add end-to-end operation-count tests for each known container and caller. Every malformed or contradictory attempted/dispatch case must stop after accessibility_action; only valid pre-dispatch and exact definite-no-effect cases may perform one fallback.

findings.title: A truncated selector query can still resolve and cache a candidate
findings.observation: The resolver records diagnostics.truncated but continues through pick, updates the cache, and returns status=resolved whenever at least one candidate was returned. It reports selector_query_truncated only when no candidate was picked.
findings.trigger: A bounded selector query returns one matching node and truncated=true because its time or node limit hides remaining candidates.
findings.impact: An unseen candidate may score higher or make the result ambiguous, so the cached element can be wrong and later receive AXPress, focus, or another semantic action.

evidence.description: A one-candidate truncated query returned 'resolved 0/2 True None' instead of failing closed.
truncated is set at lines 210-216, but the non-empty path reaches cache update and resolved at lines 316-334.
The design requires timeout/truncation diagnostics and partial output only when an explicit selector or collection policy allows it.

findings.remediation: Fail closed before picking or caching when a decision-critical selector query is truncated, unless an explicit reviewed policy can prove that partial candidates are safe for that pick mode. Do not cache a truncated selection.
findings.verification: Add candidate-present truncation tests for time and limit reasons, hidden higher-score and duplicate candidates, every pick strategy, and cache state. Unsafe cases must return selector_query_truncated with no cache entry or mutation.

findings.title: Known nested action copies are not bound to the requested action
findings.observation: The direct response action is compared with expected_action, but action, actionEffect, and nativeErrorCode in diagnostics, diagnostics.transport, and protocol evidence are outside the consistency payload set.
findings.trigger: An AXPress request receives valid top-level and nested AXPress/-25206 proof while diagnostics.action is AXSetFocus, diagnostics.actionEffect is performed, diagnostics.nativeErrorCode is -25204, or an equivalent evidence copy conflicts.
findings.impact: The response can authorize a second mutation although a known response copy contradicts the exact no-effect proof for the requested action.

evidence.description: AXPress with diagnostics.action=AXSetFocus still returned success and operations ['accessibility_action', 'click']; the evidence matrix also found 19 ignored nested/evidence contradictions.
Required action/effect/code helpers consume only _accessibility_action_proof_payloads, which excludes the known nested containers.
Every response action copy must agree and equal the outbound action; every occurrence of all proof fields must have the expected type and value.

findings.remediation: Include every supported action/effect/code occurrence in the same fail-closed consistency pass used for the request action, including diagnostics, transport, and protocol evidence. Reject malformed, empty, or contradictory containers and values.
findings.verification: Run a matrix for both AXPress and AXSetFocus over every public/metadata/nested/diagnostics/transport/evidence copy. Matching pairs may use exactly one fallback; every mismatch, malformed copy, -25204, performed/unknown effect, or wrong code must execute zero fallback.

findings.title: The committed approval result is invalid under the current review contract
findings.observation: The current validator rejects the committed f19cbd9 result for four preserved-ID fingerprint drifts, a three-dot delta range, eight uncovered reviewed paths, and six approval-required reviewer runs bound to 65f8855 rather than f19cbd9.
findings.trigger: A maintainer or automation validates the committed approval artifact or follows the downstream F6 documents that claim its schema, SHA, and internal consistency passed.

evidence.description: validate_review_result.py returned INVALID with 12 contract errors.

findings.title: Collection extraction silently ignores selector steps after the first
findings.observation: Collection item and descendant-field selectors are validated as full SelectorDefinition objects, but extraction directly chooses steps[0]. The batch path does the same, and pick/confidence/fallback/root semantics are not applied.
findings.trigger: A valid collection profile uses two selector steps such as AXGroup followed by AXStaticText for a descendant field.
findings.impact: The extractor can return a value from the wrong container, omit valid rows or fields, or attach an incorrect element reference while reporting the collection resolved.

evidence.description: A valid two-step field selector returned ({'displayName': 'WRONG-CONTAINER'},) with only three query calls; the fourth step query never ran.
_query_items uses item_selector.steps[0], _extract_field uses field.selector.steps[0], and validation accepts every non-empty step list.
The collection flow says item and field selectors are resolved relative to their roots using the selector model.

findings.remediation: Either execute collection item and field definitions through the complete selector semantics or reject every unsupported selector shape and policy at profile-validation time. Never accept configuration that runtime silently truncates.
findings.verification: Add multi-step item and field fixtures covering root, constraints, pick, confidence, fallbacks, batch/non-batch parity, and wrong-container decoys. Accepted profiles must execute all steps; unsupported profiles must fail before any query.

findings.title: Selector profile and control-map overrides do not activate atomically
findings.observation: load_selector_profile and load_control_map parse the same override independently and independently fall back. WeChatDesktopTool fixes the control map at construction while resolver builders load the selector profile separately, allowing a mixed packaged/override configuration.
findings.trigger: selector_profile_path contains an invalid selector section but a valid changed control_map, or the inverse.
findings.impact: An override rejected for semantic selection can still drive fast-path navigation or mutation with incompatible paths; the reproduced mixed state retained override path 0/99.

evidence.description: The split override loaded packaged profile wechat.macos/app-control.selector-profile.v1 while activating control-map path ('0/99',).
The selector loader falls back at profiles.py:42-48; the control-map loader separately succeeds or falls back at control_map.py:67-78; tool construction loads only the map.
The approved remediation requires invalid overrides to fall back only when selector profile and control map activate atomically.

findings.remediation: Parse and validate the selector profile and control map as one activation transaction and return both from one loader. If either section is missing or invalid, use both packaged defaults (or fail configuration) and keep one immutable pair for the tool lifetime.
findings.verification: Add both half-valid override directions, invalid TOML, missing sections, construction/reload, and fast-path tests. No test may observe components from different sources, and invalid overrides must issue no command through rejected map data.

findings.title: Collection pagination applies the caller limit before semantic acceptance
findings.observation: The extractor requests effective_limit+1 raw AX rows, computes has_more from that raw list, and never scans beyond it after required-field failures cause rows to be skipped. The public limit therefore bounds raw candidates rather than accepted semantic items.
findings.trigger: The first limit+1 AX rows include candidates rejected by required semantic fields while a later row is valid.
findings.impact: The API can return status=failed with no items even though a valid item is immediately available, while also reporting hasMore=true with nextCursor=null; callers cannot obtain the promised semantic page or advance reliably.

evidence.description: With limit=1, two rejected leading rows, and a valid third row, the engine queried only two items and returned failed/items=()/hasMore=true/nextCursor=null.
Raw lookahead is fixed at effective_limit+1 before field extraction; skipped rows only increment counters and the loop has no continuation query.
The collection contract defines caller limit and N+1 pagination over accepted semantic items.

findings.remediation: Use bounded overscan or continuation queries until effective_limit accepted semantic items plus one accepted lookahead are found, or a trustworthy visible-exhaustion condition is reached. Keep explicit query/time bounds and coherent cursor semantics.
findings.verification: Add noisy leading/middle rows with required-field rejection, later valid items, exact accepted limits, visible exhaustion, truncation, and cursor continuity. Assert bounded query counts, returned count, hasMore, nextCursor, and no hidden accepted item loss.

findings.title: Bundle targeting can execute an Accessibility action in a background app
findings.observation: When the actual frontmost application's bundle does not match the request, the generated action worker enumerates same-bundle processes and returns an active or merely usable background candidate. It then resolves that process's focused window and performs the requested AX action.
findings.trigger: Another application is frontmost while a non-terminated process for the requested bundle remains available in the background.
findings.impact: A semantic command can mutate a background application's UI despite the appFrontmost precondition, acting on stale or unintended state without the user's visible focus context.

evidence.description: A pure in-memory generated-worker probe kept TextEdit frontmost, supplied an inactive WeChat process, and still performed [('Send', 'AXPress')] with status=ok.
Both query and action generated scripts fall back from a nonmatching frontmost app to active and then merely usable same-bundle candidates.
The action lifecycle requires a current frontmost precheck, and the packaged WeChat profile declares appFrontmost=true.

findings.remediation: Before any AX query or action, require the current NSWorkspace frontmost application to match the requested bundle/name and be usable. Do not fall back to a background same-bundle process; return a structured target-not-frontmost failure without issuing an action.
findings.verification: Execute generated query/action workers against inactive, background, terminated, and multiple-instance fakes. Mismatch cases must produce zero AX actions; only the exact current frontmost target may proceed.

findings.title: Normal selector evidence and events expose raw AX content beyond the semantic limit
findings.observation: The new selector/control-map paths store complete accessibility_query observations in normal evidence. _safe_app_control_observation only redacts text/message under input, so query nodes, AX values, window titles, and descriptions also flow into progress/final events and LoggingToolObserver(redact_text=True).
findings.trigger: A bounded semantic list returns fewer accepted records than the low-level query observed, and a later node contains private contact, preview, message, title, or AX value data.
findings.impact: Data intentionally absent from the semantic response can leak through ordinary result evidence, event observers, and default redacted logs, widening disclosure to telemetry and log consumers.

evidence.description: list_contacts(limit=2) returned only Ada/Bob semantically, but PRIVATE_CANARY_CHARLIE appeared in result evidence and progress/final events.
The same canary appeared in eight lines emitted by the default LoggingToolObserver with redact_text=True.
The selector runner stores the complete sanitized observation, but the sanitizer only recursively redacts selected nested input keys before events forward it.
Normal responses and logs must exclude raw AX attributes and private contact/message/window values unless explicit private debugging is enabled.

findings.remediation: Make normal-mode app-control evidence schema-aware and allowlist only status, failure information, counts, and non-sensitive timing. Remove accessibilityQuery nodes/raw, window titles, descriptions, and AX values; raw query evidence must require explicit private-debug opt-in.
findings.verification: Use canaries beyond contact limits, in conversation previews, message bodies, and window data. Assert absence from result evidence, inspect_window(includeRaw=false), progress/final events, and LoggingToolObserver(redact_text=true), while preserving intended semantic output and explicit private-debug behavior.

findings.title: Maximum collection pages generate batch query limits rejected by the public client
findings.observation: Batch field extraction sets query.limit to len(item_paths)*step.limit without capping or chunking it. The real ComputerUseClient accepts accessibility_query limits only from 1 through 500.
findings.trigger: The packaged contacts collection requests its supported maximum page of 100 items plus lookahead and a batched field step limit of 8, producing limit=808.
findings.impact: A documented maximum-size collection request fails client normalization with ValueError before the query runs, so valid profile configuration is incompatible with the public backend contract.

evidence.description: A 101-item batch generated limit=808 while the real normalizer rejected it with 'query.limit must be between 1 and 500'.
The batch calculation is unbounded at collections.py:454; the client validator enforces MAX_ACCESSIBILITY_QUERY_LIMIT=500.

findings.remediation: Chunk or otherwise bound every generated field query to at most 500 while preserving coverage for all item-path/field combinations. Do not silently truncate items or fields to satisfy the transport limit.
findings.verification: Run packaged maximum-page collections through the real client normalizer for batch and non-batch paths, assert every generated limit is within bounds, and compare semantic output with an unbatched reference.

findings.title: WeChat selector failure routing does not treat structured diagnostics as authoritative
findings.observation: Selector and collection wrappers only special-case selector_query_failed, so selector_query_truncated falls into generic not-found routing. For query failures, the structured cause is concatenated with free-text message content and keyword-classified, allowing unrelated message words to override the known cause.
findings.trigger: A selector query is truncated, or diagnostics carry a known transport cause while the free-text message contains permission-related words (or the inverse).
findings.impact: Callers receive the wrong top-level status, failureKind, retryability, and recovery hint; truncation can look like missing content and transport failures can direct users to change Accessibility permissions.

evidence.description: A helper_transport_failed cause plus 'Permission denied' message mapped to missing_accessibility, while selector_query_truncated mapped to not_found/main_content_not_found.
Only selector_query_failed takes the structured mapper, and that mapper classifies a concatenation of cause and diagnostic_message by substring order.
The design maps selector_query_truncated to wechat_query_truncated and defines cause-specific recovery guidance.

findings.remediation: Map every known failure_kind and cause_failure_kind by exact structured value, including selector_query_truncated. Use free-text heuristics only when the structured cause is absent or explicitly unknown, and never let message content override a known cause.
findings.verification: Add selector/collection matrices for permission, timeout, helper/local-service/socket transport, and limit/time-budget truncation. Give each case an adversarial message containing another category's keywords and assert top-level status, failure kind, retryability, hint, and nested diagnostics.

findings.title: New query and action worker failures are absent from the stable package registry
findings.observation: Warm query/action workers emit four package-owned failures—accessibility_query_worker_failed, accessibility_query_worker_empty_response, accessibility_action_worker_failed, and accessibility_action_worker_empty_response—and the client preserves them as top-level failureKind values, but none is declared in COMPUTER_USE_FAILURE_KINDS.
findings.trigger: A warm worker raises before producing a result or exits without a response and a tuple-based public consumer routes the normalized ToolObservation.
findings.impact: Stable-registry consumers cannot classify real package-owned failures and may treat them as unknown or violate exhaustive routing assumptions.

evidence.description: Real query/action wrapper failures normalized to accessibility_*_worker_failed with registered=False for both observations.
The worker scripts produce four strings and the client preserves them, while errors.py declares no constants or tuple members for them.
The public package contract advertises stable package-owned failure routing through COMPUTER_USE_FAILURE_KINDS.

findings.remediation: Declare and export constants for all four worker failure values and add them once to COMPUTER_USE_FAILURE_KINDS. Keep producer, normalizer, and stable registry synchronized.
findings.verification: Exercise query/action worker failure and empty-response paths, assert top-level registry membership for all four values, public wheel imports, tuple uniqueness, and release-preflight coverage.

findings.title: The real native unsupported producer now includes action
findings.observation: Generated post-call failures now carry the validated requested action through ComputerUseClient normalization.
findings.trigger: The direct backend returns AXPress/-25206 or AXSetFocus/-25205.
findings.impact: Both valid native unsupported cases can preserve exactly one configured compatibility fallback.

evidence.description: Current-head production-generated worker tests for both native pairs and operation counts pass.
Exact-head GitHub CI passed the package suites.

findings.remediation: Completed at the current head: emit and preserve action in native post-call failure results.
findings.verification: Both real generated native pairs retain one configured fallback; uncertain or mismatched results retain none.

findings.title: The new package failure remains in the stable routing tuple
findings.observation: ACCESSIBILITY_ACTION_UNSUPPORTED owns the emitted value and remains included in COMPUTER_USE_FAILURE_KINDS.
findings.trigger: A direct native unsupported action result is routed by a tuple-based package consumer.
findings.impact: The result remains classifiable through the advertised stable package failure contract.

evidence.description: Both real normalized failure kinds satisfy registry membership assertions and the current package suite passes.

findings.remediation: Completed and preserved at the current head.
findings.verification: Keep producer, normalization, registry, and public tuple tests green.
